subject: Oceanography
title: Microfossils as Climate Records
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Microfossils as Climate Records.

hook.text: A single gram of deep-sea sediment can contain thousands of microfossils—each one a climate time capsule.

buildup.text: Foraminifera and diatoms build shells that preserve the chemistry of the water they lived in.

discovery.text: Oxygen isotope ratios in their shells reveal ancient ocean temperatures and global ice volume.

twist.text: By analyzing species assemblages, scientists can reconstruct ancient ocean circulation patterns.

climax.text: Microfossil records now extend back 200 million years—a detailed archive of Earth's climate swings.

punchline.text: Tiny shells hold the memory of ancient climates.

quiz.question: What do oxygen isotopes in foraminifera reveal?
options: Past ocean temperatures and ice volume
